name: Interface, Controlled Edit & Localization Image Prompts
body: # Interfaces, controlled edits, and localization Ten Qwen Image 3.0 prompt recipes. Replace bracketed inputs before generation. All quoted text is exact; no translation is implied unless explicitly requested. Outputs require human review. ## DIG-01 — Tool library mobile interface ```text Create a 16:9 board showing three mobile screens for fictional app "Borrow Bench": catalog, item detail and reservation confirmation. Use ivory backgrounds, navy type, teal action buttons and consistent rounded cards. Show a yellow drill as the selected item. Render only "Borrow Bench", "Find a tool", "Cordless drill", "Reserve", "Collection time", "Saturday 10:00", "Reservation saved", and "View booking" in their appropriate screens. No prices, personal information or extra navigation labels. This is a static interface concept; do not imply functioning controls. ``` ## DIG-02 — CSV import review screen ```text Create a 16:9 desktop interface mockup for fictional inventory app "Stockroom". Show an import review table with columns "Item", "Quantity", and "Status"; include three supplied sample rows, one visibly marked "Needs review". Above the table render "Review your import"; below it place "Back" and "Import valid rows" buttons. Use a clean white layout with amber error emphasis and a readable sidebar containing only "Inventory". Preserve supplied data and do not display personal information. Variables: sample rows and approved copy. ``` ## DIG-03 — Regional rail homepage ```text Create a 16:9 desktop homepage concept for fictional travel planner "Local Lines". Use a large coastal-train photograph on the right and a practical search panel on the left. Render exactly "Take the slower route", "From", "To", "Travel date", and "Find journeys"; keep fields empty. Use cream background, dark-green controls and generous spacing. Add no real schedules, fares, operator logos or availability claims. Keep the train physically plausible and interface text separate from the photograph. Variables: region imagery and approved headline. ``` ## DIG-04 — Cooperative game HUD ```text Create a 16:9 static HUD concept for a fictional mountain-delivery game. Keep the central sixty percent of a snowy trail unobstructed. Place a compact compass at the top, two teammate status bars at the upper left and three inventory slots at the lower right. Render only "North", "Team", "Parcel", "Rope", and "Map". Use high-contrast shapes with restrained amber highlights, not cinematic floating holograms. Avoid real military insignia, unreadable microtext and excessive overlays. Variables: game setting and approved labels. ``` ## DIG-05 — Poster text replacement ```text Use Image 1 as the edit target and [APPROVED SOURCE-TO-TARGET TEXT MAP] as the only replacement copy. Replace the specified poster words without changing photography, illustrations, palette, margins, logos or non-target text. Preserve type weight and hierarchy; adjust line breaks only where the target language requires it. Keep punctuation, accents and reading direction correct. Remove the old words rather than duplicating them. Do not translate unspecified text or add explanations. Variables: source image and complete text map. ``` ## DIG-06 — Photo damage repair ```text Use one authorized scanned photograph as the edit target. Repair only visible dust, scratches and fold damage, reconstructing small missing areas from neighboring texture. Preserve identity, age, expression, crop, clothing, original grain and tonal range. Do not colorize a monochrome source, smooth skin, open eyes or invent background objects. Keep uncertain large missing regions unchanged rather than hallucinating details. Output one restored image without comparison labels or watermark. Variables: source photograph and explicitly marked repair areas. ``` ## DIG-07 — Three-reference product composite ```text Use Image 1 as the base tabletop scene, Image 2 as the exact ceramic cup reference and Image 3 only as the glaze-color reference. Place one cup from Image 2 on the empty coaster in Image 1 and apply only the supplied glaze hue. Preserve the base camera, crop, surrounding objects and cup geometry. Match light direction, contact shadow, perspective and reflections. Do not copy objects or text from Image 3. Add no text. Variables: three authorized images and intended cup placement. ``` ## DIG-08 — Sketch to reading room ```text Use an approved room sketch as the layout reference. Create a 4:3 realistic reading-room concept with pale oak shelves, a moss-green bench and diffuse ceiling light. Preserve every wall, window, doorway and furniture footprint from the sketch; use the material palette only to finish existing surfaces. Keep perspective coherent and aisle widths visually unchanged. Add no people, extra furniture, plants or signs. This is an illustrative concept, not a measured construction drawing. Variables: sketch and approved materials. ``` ## DIG-09 — Accessible empty state ```text Create a 3:4 mobile interface mockup for an empty saved-reading list. Use a cream background, navy text and one small illustration of three closed books. Render exactly "Nothing saved yet", "Keep useful reads in one place", and "Explore articles". Place the explanation beneath the heading and a large button below; leave comfortable margins. Use high contrast and no tiny text, loading skeleton, fake article cards or notification badges. This is a static design proposal; accessibility still requires implementation testing. ``` ## DIG-10 — Language direction comparison ```text Create a 16:9 side-by-side interface typography board from [APPROVED ENGLISH AND ARABIC COPY]. The left panel uses left-to-right alignment; the right uses natural right-to-left alignment. Preserve the same component hierarchy, spacing and two button roles while adapting reading order. Keep product photographs unchanged rather than mirroring them. Render only supplied strings, with connected Arabic glyphs and intact Latin brand names. No transliteration, duplicate source text or invented copy. Variables: paired strings and component labels; require fluent Arabic review. ``` [Back to the prompt index](./README.md).
description_en: Ten Qwen Image 3.0 recipes for app-screen mockups, controlled image edits and multilingual layouts, listing every UI string to render and nothing else.
description_zh: 十条面向 Qwen Image 3.0 的界面与本地化出图配方，用于 App 界面示意图、受控图像编辑与多语言排版，逐条列出需渲染的界面文案，多一个字都不加。
long_en: Interface recipes lay out multi-screen boards or desktop mockups with a fixed palette, then enumerate the exact strings for each screen — nav labels, table columns, button text — and forbid prices, personal data or extra navigation. They also require the image to read as a static concept rather than imply working controls. Localization recipes carry supplied text across languages without silently translating what was marked exact.
long_zh: 界面类配方规定多屏展示板或桌面端示意图的版式与配色，随后逐条列出每屏要渲染的确切文案——导航标签、表格列名、按钮文字——并禁止出现价格、个人信息或额外导航项，同时要求画面读起来是静态概念稿而非可交互控件。本地化类配方负责把提供的文案跨语言呈现，且不会擅自翻译被标为「原样保留」的内容。
sec_note_en: Plain text prompts; no tool access or external calls. Mockups are pictures, not designs you can hand to engineering — text in generated UI often needs correcting by hand, especially in non-Latin scripts. Written for Qwen Image 3.0; the repo is curated by the commercial platform bestimage.ai, though the prompt files carry no product placement.
sec_note_zh: 纯文本提示词，不涉及工具调用或外部请求。生成的只是界面「图片」而非可交付给研发的设计稿——画面中的文字往往需要人工校正，非拉丁文字尤其如此。针对 Qwen Image 3.0 撰写；来源仓库由商业平台 bestimage.ai 维护，提示词文件本身无产品植入。
